memo.verdict: Neutral at 30.96 EUR (2026-09-24); bullish at or below 30 EUR, the price at which the modal path clears 20% a year over eighteen months (29.8 EUR at 16.0x; 30.2 EUR at the blended 16.2x; 27.4 EUR on the three-year test). Progress to Early-Stage rather than park. Conviction: medium on the business and the demand; a working hypothesis on the return, because the return leg rests on the interest line and the sector's multiple, neither of which the company controls. The park rule does not bite: no D or F on management ('No mediocre management' B), business quality ('Business' B), predictability ('Transmission' B) or trackability ('Leading indicators' C). Triggers named: a book-to-bill below 1.0x at the 9 November 2026 trading update or at FY2026, or the 902 EURm of options not exercised through the Q4 2026 season; a reported half-year adjusted EBIT margin below 26% (Invalidate); gross margin below 33% (Alarm); net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x at late 2027 with no asset sale under way (Invalidate), or at or above 3.5x, the covenant (Invalidate); a new acquisition before HGH is integrated (Alarm); tube lead times above 20 months, Harder below 15,000 tubes, net working capital above 43% of revenue, Kappa below 35 EURm in FY2026 (Alarms).
case: - The thesis: Theon is a contracted demand-inflection case in European soldier optronics, compelling at the operating line and only adequate at the shareholder's line at 30.96 EUR. The company has turned a policy-backed rearmament cycle into a 1.46 EURbn backlog and a 26.2% margin, but financed its expansion with 8.6m new shares and about 550 EURm of peak net debt, so EBITDA growing at about 30% a year reaches EPS at about 20%, and the modal return is about 17% a year over eighteen months and 15% over three years against the 20% bar. At about 30 EUR, 3% below the price, the modal path clears the bar.

- The external force is sector-wide, structural and contracted. European order intake across Morgan Stanley's coverage +25% to over 85 EURbn, aggregate backlog a record 438 EURbn (September 2026); NATO 5% of GDP by 2035 with 3.5% core; Germany 180 EURbn by 2030; SAFE 150 EURbn; militaries moving to one-to-one soldier equipping. Theon's 1 EURbn OCCAR framework (100,000 devices for Germany, 4,000 for Belgium, December 2025) is the largest night-vision procurement in NATO history. Direction by force: demand tailwind intensifying; core competition mild tailwind (the US primes ITAR-blocked, the European primes avoid Theon's markets), headwind at the platform and upstream edges; regulation tailwind (Buy-European 35% non-EU component cap, EU design authority, Omnibus V ten-year frameworks); own cycle turning up (experts' peak 2028 to 2029); macro neutral except the cost of money; supply side headwind D; the sector multiple a headwind to the price (C).

- The internal change is broad and leverage-funded: guidance raised twice in 2026 (A); balance-sheet utilisation B with the 'dangerous leverage' flag partly present (0.4x to 0.5x of covenant headroom); strategy pivot to 50/50 by 2029 resourced (B, empire-building flag plausible, five transactions in twelve months); acquisitions coherent and delivering (Kappa 11 points of H1 growth, a 42 EURm order) but discipline unproven at HGH's price (B); new products A (PHYLAX over 40 EURm, Kappa 42 EURm plus 27 EURm options, 100 EURm thermal clip-on, 70 EURm IdZ, record 25 EURm Harder third-party order); new geographies B (Europe still 83.1% of backlog); standards B; shareholder returns D (payout cut to 20% to 30%, rights issue at 30% discount); the Exosens reversal C; price rises C (industry prices up 2.5x to 3.0x since 2022 but passed through back-to-back, OCCAR "priced competitively"); no chief-executive change (D, an absence); perimeter widening (F, an absence).
counter_case: - At the whole-case level: Theon is a cyclical peak bought with leverage. European soldier-equipment demand is a two-to-three-year replenishment surge that peaks in 2027 to 2029, as the company's own former managers say; the largest contract is an agency framework priced for volume, and agency buying rises to 40% of European procurement by 2030, so the 26% margin is a pre-OCCAR artefact that compresses to the 15% to 18% the experts expect as volumes roll off; the founder has spent the peak's cash and about 550 EURm of debt on a supplier's minority stake with no control, a French acquisition at 18.5x EBITDA and a scatter of platform and AI ventures where Theon has no proven edge; free cash flow on FactSet's definition was 16.9% of net income in FY2025 and working capital eats 41 cents of every revenue euro; the balance sheet reaches 3.0x to 3.1x against a 3.5x covenant in the very quarter a ceasefire could delay the tranches; and the precedent for the fix is a rights issue at a 30% discount. On that reading the stock de-rates from 16.4x on peak earnings to the crash band of 10.1x on falling ones, 19.1 EUR or lower, and Deutsche Bank's free-cash-flow-yield value of 18.00 EUR is the honest number. The sector has already de-rated 20% to 38% over twelve months.

- Conceded: the timing of the leverage is poor and self-inflicted; the free-cash-flow record on any definition but the company's is weak; the Exosens stake is a governance oddity we would not have made; the R&D budget (2.8% of revenue) does not support the software ambition; the drop-through sensitivity shows the modal return falling to a D on a modest adverse ratio.
triggers: - Backlog conversion: a book-to-bill below 1.0x at the 9 November 2026 update or at FY2026, or the 902 EURm of options not exercised through the Q4 2026 season, would change the view; the record puts conversion at about 75%.

- Margin: a reported half-year adjusted EBIT margin below 26% invalidates; gross margin below 33% is the alarm; the record puts the margin holding at about 70%; the experts' 15% to 18% at the cycle's peak is the skew.

- Deleveraging: net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x at late 2027 (the H1 2027 report in September 2027 is the named check) with no asset sale under way invalidates; at or above 3.5x, the covenant, invalidates at any time; a new acquisition before HGH is integrated is the alarm; the record puts deleveraging at about 65%.

- The multiple: no sector de-rating inside eighteen months is put at 55%, so a de-rating is plausible; the re-rating needs both a cleaner balance sheet and a sector that stops falling, and neither is given better than two-to-one.
- Tube supply: lead times above 20 months or Harder below 15,000 tubes are the alarms; the record puts supply holding to 2030 at about 80%.
- Other alarms: net working capital above 43% of revenue; Kappa revenue below 35 EURm in FY2026.

judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** F. Defence. Industry RS 13 at the Friday 2 October reading (20 the week before; 13 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** F.2. Defence, non-primes. Sector RS 12 at the 30 September month-end (23 four weeks earlier). Its other companies: Exail Technologies (Stock RS 62), Exosens (61), Hensoldt (34), Kongsberg Gruppen (31), Montana Aerospace (26), Melrose Industries (18), and 4 more
- **Cohort:** European defence electronics, sensors and command systems. The cohort's relative strength 32 (32 four weeks earlier), 5 companies: MilDef (94), Exosens (61), Hensoldt (34), Ovzon (7)


**What is going on, and why it matters**

- **The price move by beta:** over 5 sessions the stock rose 1.8% to EUR 29.76; the market's fall explains -0.7%, so its own move was +2.4%, under half its usual size (about 6.9%).
  - Over 20 sessions it fell 8.7%, an own move of -6.6%, about six tenths of its usual size: it fell on five straight sessions from 24 to 30 September. The dated news: on 30 September the company announced about EUR 50 million of new orders and pre-selection for higher-value contracts and options, and the shares fell 0.8% that day
  - Good news no longer lifts it
- **The sector and cohort:** Industry RS 13 puts defence near the bottom of the universe's relative-strength ranking; Theon's own Stock RS fell from 69 at the end of August to 19 at the month-end, the fastest collapse in the book, while its cohort held at 32: the market is leaving the sector and leaving Theon faster than its peers
- **The analysts:** Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates +22% but target prices -11% (from +10% at the end of August): more analysts cut their target price than raised it in the last 100 days. With Stock RS below 50, that meets the fourth criterion; Sell-side Momentum fell to C from B

**What it means for the position**

- **Holding:** held only by your one-off link: five of the six Sell Criteria are met (Industry RS 13; the 200-day slope -0.2%; Sector RS 12 with Stock RS 19; Stock RS 19 with target-price breadth below zero; relative price 27% below its 52-week high). Without the link the rule sells it today
- **Selling:** first in the order of sale, so today's first purchase releases it. If no purchase is made, the only exit that acts on it is the 30% level at EUR 26.82, about 10% below (one level for both tranches); *plausible within weeks*, because its usual own move over 20 sessions is 11%
- **Adding:** not allowed (a criterion has fired) and not wanted
- **Its place in the order of sale:** first, because it meets more criteria than any other holding, including both the one that measures its own trend (the slope) and the one that measures its own analysts (target-price cuts), as well as the three group readings.
  - What would move it down: a Stock RS back above 50 at the 30 October reading with the slope positive, or a 9 November trading update with book-to-bill above 1.0 and the OCCAR options exercised.
  - What we lose by waiting: 0.40% of capital if the 30% level is hit, and 4.05% of capital held in one of the weakest industries in the universe

**What we could lose:** about 0.40% of the fund's capital, to the 30% level, the only exit that acts on it under the link (the relative 52W high trigger at EUR 28.24, 5% below, has already fired and no longer sells it)

**Experiment: which stocks Theon's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)

- **Exosens** (same sector and cohort): 0.64 and 0.55, strong
- **Hensoldt** (same sector and cohort): 0.38 and 0.43, moderate
- **MilDef** (same sector and cohort): 0.38 and 0.34, moderate
- **Kongsberg Gruppen** (same sector): 0.34 and 0.36, moderate
- **My reading:** look at Exosens first; the two optronics names move together, and Exosens (Stock RS 61) has held up where Theon has not

**The Investment Analyst's memo (digest of 25 September at EUR 30.96; memo republished 1 October)**

- **Decided:** neutral at EUR 30.96 and bullish at or below EUR 30, the price at which the modal path clears 20% a year over eighteen months; progress to Early-Stage rather than park; conviction medium on the business, a working hypothesis on the return; gates management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C
- **Must happen:** the EUR 1.46 billion backlog converts (book-to-bill above 1.0 at the 9 November update; the EUR 902 million of options exercised through the fourth quarter); a half-year adjusted EBIT margin above 26%; net debt below 2.5 times EBITDA by late 2027
- **Main risk:** a cyclical peak bought with leverage: European soldier-equipment demand peaks in 2027 to 2029 and the 26% margin compresses to 15% to 18% as agency buying rises
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** just short of our 20% a year bar at EUR 30.96; clears it at or below EUR 30. <u>At Monday's EUR 29.76 the shares are below the memo's bullish level, so the Investment Analyst's view and the rule now disagree: the memo would buy here, the rule sells</u>
- **Next test:** the trading update on 9 November (book-to-bill; the options)

**My judgement:** bearish on the position, medium conviction: five signals describe a stock the market has left, and the price fell through the memo's bullish level because the demand case is being re-priced by the whole sector, not because the case was tested and passed; sell first when a purchase releases it. The rule governs a Core Investment

- If you keep it, the memo's EUR 30 level is the reason you would record.
- **Counter-case:** the demand is contracted (a EUR 1 billion framework, a EUR 1.46 billion backlog, NATO spending targets to 2035) and at EUR 29.76 our own analyst's path clears 20% a year
  - The five criteria are relative-strength readings on a sector rotation, not on the company, so selling here sells at the bottom of a rotation, and a 9 November update with book-to-bill above 1.0 would show the rule sold a working case

**What would change my view:** the 30 October readings (Stock RS above 50 and the slope above zero would clear two criteria); the 9 November trading update (book-to-bill above 1.0; the options exercised); a close below EUR 26.82, where the tranche rule sells regardless of the link
